subtask: Provider Result → human Review → bounded Local Revision → second human Review → receipt/output/revision hash lineage

requirements.summary: The operational provider surface now executes both root provider jobs and nested local-revision provider jobs through the same Adapter Registry → Executor Bridge → ProviderExecutor path. Local revision execution is no longer an out-of-band manual gap.

Provider execution materializes output bytes, production receipt and SHA256 lineage; machine quality/reference observations are required before COMPLETE, and addressable output Review must be explicitly accepted before final actual-output closure.

A human REVISE decision creates a bounded revision request, compiles a revision-scoped provider job, executes it through the same provider surface, records changed fields/layers and revised-output SHA, then requires an addressable second Review before ACCEPTED lineage.

The production/review/revision lineage is persisted with explicit human acceptance and is wired into the existing learning-loop authority. Phase 8 proves the production/review/revision side of the loop, but does not falsely claim a fresh real measurement→learning cycle E2E run.

The Phase 7 final semantic/package boundary is preserved and its actual-output boundary can now be driven to E2E_PROVEN by an executed lifecycle inside CBCC: provider result bytes + production receipt/output hashes + accepted output Review + executed bounded Local Revision + revised-output hash + accepted revision Review. Fresh K01 FULL and authenticated installed Host-native parity remain later locked phases.

verified_behavior: Root provider jobs and Local Revision provider jobs execute through the same ProviderAdapterRegistry and ProviderExecutorBridge instead of treating local revision execution as an external/manual hole.
The CLI exposes revision-execute without accepting or persisting provider credentials; credentials/callbacks remain host-injected runtime context.
Provider output bytes are materialized and SHA256-checked against the production receipt before the result can participate in the actual-output boundary.

For locked/reference product routes, provider quality observations must include product identity/reference/source-hash evidence. Missing evidence remains REVIEW_REQUIRED; human acceptance cannot silently substitute for missing machine evidence.

A bounded human REVISE decision preserves allowed_fields/allowed_layers, executes a nested provider job, materializes revised output bytes, computes revised_output_hash, and requires an explicit revision-output Review.

The exact Phase 7 package-side audit_actual_output_boundary changes from E2E_PENDING to E2E_PROVEN only when provider result, both Reviews, Local Revision and lineage hashes are all present and valid.

Legacy v0.6.16 host-surface tests were upgraded to the current quality-evidence contract and pass together with the Phase 8 tests, proving the stricter evidence contract did not require weakening the provider runtime.

honesty_boundary.reason: Phase 8 proves the CBCC provider/result/review/revision/hash lifecycle with actual materialized bytes through the production provider execution boundary. It does not fabricate an external vendor/network call or authenticated installed-plugin Host origin.

invariants: Provider job existence is not Provider Result proof.
Human ACCEPT does not override missing machine quality/reference evidence.
Local Revision must be bounded to the approved smallest responsible fields/layers and must preserve parent package lineage.
Revision output is independently reviewable and cannot self-accept.
Phase 8 does not satisfy Fresh K01 FULL Phase 10 or authenticated installed Host-native Phase 11.
